montecristo-cuba--linea-clasica.description: The original Montecristo blend, made in Havana since 1935 and long treated as the reference for Cuban flavour. Totally handmade with long filler, it smokes medium to full with the brand's distinctive aroma, from the small No. 4 to the tapered No. 2.

thirds.notes: A delicate, creamy opening of cedar and wood with gentle spice.
Coffee, leather and cocoa build in, softened by a honeyed sweetness.
The most intense third: pepper and earth over a lingering dark-chocolate sweetness.

sources.title: Habanos press release – Montecristo Línea Clásica (via halfwheel)

montecristo-cuba--linea-open.description: Introduced in 2009, Línea Open was conceived to be smoked outdoors, with the Eagle, Master, Regata and Junior as the first vitolas. It is made totally by hand in Havana with long filler from Vuelta Abajo, and Habanos rates it medium, a step lighter than the Montecristo classics.

sources.title: Cigar Inspector – Montecristo Open Master review
Cigars Lover – Montecristo Open Master review
Stogie Review – Montecristo Open Eagle and Junior

thirds.notes: A round, woody start with cedar, a little earth and soft white pepper, without any sharp kick.
Wood stays in charge as coffee and a slightly bitter spice appear, carried by a smooth, creamy smoke.
Little changes: wood and coffee hold to the end, with pepper in the background and the smoke still creamy.

montecristo-cuba--linea-1935.description: Named after the year Montecristo was founded at the H. Upmann factory in Havana, Línea 1935 adds three vitolas to the regular range: Maltés, Dumas and Leyenda. Habanos presents it as the most premium part of the brand, made totally by hand with Vuelta Abajo leaf.

sources.title: Cigar Inspector – Montecristo Maltés Línea 1935 review
Cigars Lover – Montecristo Línea 1935 Dumas review
Cigars Lover – Montecristo Línea 1935 Leyenda review

thirds.notes: Wood and earth set a calm, balanced base, touched by white pepper and a roasted coffee finish.
Pepper and warmer spice build through the middle and make the blend more layered and less smooth.
Earth and roasted coffee lead the close, with wood and a grassy note; the larger Maltés grows strongest here.

montecristo-cuba--linea-clasica-stopgeze.description: This entry groups Montecristo vitolas that have left the regular catalogue, including the No. 6, the No. 7 and the Montecristo B. They followed the classic Montecristo blend of Vuelta Abajo long filler, totally handmade in Havana, and survive today mainly as aged boxes.

montecristo-cuba--edicion-limitada.description: Montecristo has been part of the Habanos Limited Edition programme since its first year, with sizes the brand does not normally make: from the Robustos of 2000 and the Montecristo C and D to the Dantés of 2016 and the Encantos of 2025. Limited Editions use tobacco aged at least two years and carry an extra dated band.

montecristo-cuba--reserva-en-gran-reserv.description: In 2007 Montecristo presented a Reserva in which wrapper, binder and filler were all aged for three years, as a tribute to the No. 4. The brand's first Gran Reserva followed in 2011: a No. 2 from the 2005 harvest. A later Edmundo Reserva uses leaf from the 2018 harvest.

montecristo-cuba--coleccion-habanos-en-s.description: Montecristo is one of the brands most often honoured in Habanos' special productions: small, one-time releases such as Colección Habanos cabinets, anniversary vitolas and humidors. Examples include the 80 Aniversario of 2015, the Churchills Añejados, the Gran Pirámides and, more recently, the Preciosos and Venerables.
